profile.aids: Closed book. A simple calculator is allowed.
profile.negativeMarking: Part A: +2 for a correct answer, −2 for a wrong one, 0 for blank. Only answer when you are sure.
rules: Justify every answer in part B; a bare result scores 0.
Show intermediate steps; they carry most of the points.
profile.passRule: At least 30 points in part B and a total of at least 55.

tasks.title: True/False on core definitions
tasks.why: On every paper and pure recall. But a wrong answer costs as much as a right one earns.
graders: Only the True/False mark is graded; no explanation is read.
A wrong answer scores −2, so leave a statement blank unless you can name the rule or a counterexample.
recipe: For each statement, look for the hidden word: every, square, rows vs columns.
True only if you can name the theorem; False only if you can name a counterexample.

tasks.title: Determinant of a 3×3 matrix
tasks.why: On every paper and routine, so the points are cheap.
graders: The expansion with its signs is worth half the points, even if the final value is off.
recipe: Pick the row or column with the most zeros.
Expand: \(\det A=\sum_j (-1)^{i+j}a_{ij}M_{ij}\), where \(M_{ij}\) deletes row \(i\) and column \(j\).
Check the sign pattern \(+,-,+\) before adding.

tasks.title: Inverse of a 2×2 matrix
tasks.why: One formula. The only trap is forgetting to check that \(\det\ne0\).
graders: The check \(AA^{-1}=I\) is a separate point.
recipe: Compute \(\det=ad-bc\). If it is 0, there is no inverse.

tasks.title: Eigenvalues, eigenvectors and definiteness
tasks.why: Worth more than the others, but the characteristic polynomial needs care.
graders: Each eigenvector must be checked with \(Av=\lambda v\) for its point.
The definiteness conclusion needs a reason (the signs of the eigenvalues).
recipe: For each \(\lambda\), solve \((A-\lambda I)v=0\) and check \(Av=\lambda v\).
All \(\lambda>0\): positive definite. Mixed signs: indefinite.

T1.intro: Decide for each statement whether it is true or false. \(A\) and \(B\) are real \(n\times n\) matrices unless stated otherwise.

parts.label: a
parts.question: Every square matrix has an inverse.
parts.solution: Counterexample: the zero matrix (or any matrix with \(\det A=0\)).

parts.label: c
parts.question: If \(Ax=0\) has only the solution \(x=0\), then \(A\) is invertible.
parts.solution: For a square matrix, a trivial null space means full rank, so \(A\) is invertible.

parts.label: d
parts.question: The eigenvalues of a triangular matrix are its diagonal entries.
parts.solution: \(\det(A-\lambda I)\) is the product of the diagonal entries \(a_{ii}-\lambda\).

parts.label: e
parts.question: For an \(m\times n\) matrix, \(\operatorname{rank}A+\operatorname{nullity}A=m\).
parts.solution: The rank–nullity theorem gives \(n\), the number of columns. The hidden word is "rows".

items.text: Expansion along a row or column with the correct signs

parts.question: Find \(A^{-1}\) for \(A=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\5&3\end{pmatrix}\), and verify your answer.
parts.solution:
1. \(\det A=2\cdot3-1\cdot5=1\ne0\), so the inverse exists.
  2. Swap and negate, divide by 1: \(\begin{pmatrix}3&-1\\-5&2\end{pmatrix}\).
  3. Check: \(\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\5&3\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}3&-1\\-5&2\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}\).

T4.intro: Let \(A=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\1&2\end{pmatrix}\). The figure shows the unit square and its image under \(A\).

items.text: Trace and determinant (or \(\det(A-\lambda I)\) written out)

parts.label: b
parts.question: Find the eigenvalues and an eigenvector for each.

parts.label: c
parts.question: Is \(A\) positive definite? Explain.
parts.solution: \(A\) is symmetric and both eigenvalues (1 and 3) are positive, so \(A\) is positive definite. In the figure, \(A\) stretches every direction without flipping it.
